questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_I
questions.learningObjective: rank organic and inorganic acids by strength using conjugate-base stability and pKa trends
questions.stem: Which of NH4+ (ammonium), HCl (hydrochloric acid), HNO3 (nitric acid), or HF (hydrofluoric acid) is the strongest acid?

options.misconception: ammonium: nitrogen holds its proton fairly tightly, so it is a weak acid
nitric acid: its conjugate base is resonance-stabilized over three oxygens, giving a low pKa
HF: the very strong H-F bond keeps it weak despite fluorine's electronegativity

questions.explanation: Among NH4+ (ammonium),HCl (hydrochloric acid),HNO3 (nitric acid),HF (hydrofluoric acid), HCl (hydrochloric acid) is the strongest acid because its conjugate base is the most stabilized, which lowers its pKa and favors proton loss.
questions.hint: The strongest acid has the lowest pKa and the most stabilized conjugate base.
